key_insight: Jointly modeling interleaved semantic, acoustic, and text tokens with native next-token audio prediction enables a single foundation model to capture both high-level content and low-level audio detail, improving general audio generation and cross-modal capabilities.
problem_solved: Overcomes limitations of text-first or semantic-only audio models that fail to represent fine acoustic detail and restrict general audio modeling and generation.
method: Train a native audio foundation model using autoregressive next-token prediction applied to audio, not just text.
Encode audio as interleaved token streams that combine semantic tokens, acoustic-detail tokens, and optional text tokens for joint modeling.
Scale and systematically evaluate the approach across tasks to quantify trade-offs between semantic fidelity, acoustic realism, and cross-modal performance.
impact: Provides a scalable, unified approach for richer audio synthesis and better multimodal integration, enabling practitioners to build generative and cross-modal audio systems that preserve both meaning and acoustic nuance.
visual_elements: Schematic timeline showing interleaved token streams (semantic | acoustic | text) aligned with waveform/spectrogram.
Side-by-side bar chart comparing semantic-only vs interleaved models on metrics for content accuracy and acoustic realism.
Pipeline diagram: raw audio → tokenization (semantic/acoustic/text) → next-token model → decoded audio/text.
Qualitative audio example panel: waveform/spectrogram + decoded semantic transcript + listening-quality indicator.
paper_title: Scaling Open Discrete Audio Foundation Models with Interleaved Semantic, Acoustic, and Text Tokens
paper_authors: Potsawee Manakul, Woody Haosheng Gan, Martijn Bartelds, Guangzhi Sun, William Held
